instructions: Soak 8 bamboo skewers in water. Cut the chicken into 1 1/2 inch pieces.
Toss the chicken in a bowl with a pinch of salt, a pinch of pepper and 1 tbsp of the mirin. Let it sit for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, mince the garlic and grate the ginger. In a small bowl, stir the soy sauce, oyster sauce, garlic, ginger, sugar, corn syrup and the remaining 3 tbsp mirin until the sugar dissolves.
Cut the white and light green parts of the scallions into 1 1/2 inch pieces. Thread the chicken and scallion pieces onto the skewers, alternating them and leaving a small gap between pieces.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook 3 or 4 skewers at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until they're lightly charred and cooked through. Transfer them to a plate and add the rest of the oil for the next batch.
Return all the skewers to the pan and lower the heat to medium-low. Pour in the glaze and turn the skewers, brushing the glaze over them, until it thickens into a glossy coat, 2 to 3 minutes.
You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut into a piece and it's done when there's no pink left.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and serve warm.
method_notes: Sources agree on boneless thigh pieces threaded with Korean leek or scallion, seared, then brushed with a sticky glaze. The lead glazes with soy, oyster sauce, mirin and corn syrup, and cooks on the stove in 30 minutes; other versions marinate for 2 hours or more and finish on a grill, or use a gochujang glaze. Heat is left out here, so add gochujang or chili flakes at the table. The lead is written for 3, so amounts are scaled up by about a third.
